title: GitHub - morvanvivien/pytrends-cloud: Drop-in replacement for the archived pytrends: same TrendReq API and pandas DataFrames, no more Google Trends 429 errors.
excerpt: Drop-in replacement for the archived pytrends: same TrendReq API and pandas DataFrames, no more Google Trends 429 errors. - morvanvivien/pytrends-cloud
content_html:
A drop-in replacement for pytrends, the Google Trends library for Python. Same TrendReq class, same methods and the same pandas DataFrames, but the requests to Google run in the cloud behind rotating proxies, so this no longer stops your script:

pytrends.exceptions.TooManyRequestsError: The request failed: Google returned a response with code 429

The original pytrends repository is archived and no longer maintained, while Google keeps rate-limiting it. pytrends-cloud keeps your code and swaps the transport.

Change one line

# from pytrends.request import TrendReq
from pytrends_cloud import TrendReq

pytrends = TrendReq(hl="en-US", tz=360)  # reads your APIFY_TOKEN, see below
pytrends.build_payload(["python", "javascript", "rust"], timeframe="today 12-m")
pytrends.interest_over_time().tail(3)

Real output, run on 14 November 2026:

            python  javascript  rust  isPartial
date
2026-10-25      34           4    15      False
2026-11-01      33           4    16      False
2026-11-08      31           4    15       True

Install

pip install pytrends-cloud

Python 3.9 or newer. Dependencies: requests and pandas, like pytrends.

Get a token (free)

  1. Create a free Apify account: https://console.apify.com/sign-up
  2. Copy your API token: https://console.apify.com/settings/integrations
  3. Set it once:
export APIFY_TOKEN="apify_api_..."      # Windows PowerShell: $env:APIFY_TOKEN = "apify_api_..."

or pass it directly: TrendReq(apify_token="apify_api_...").

What it costs

Each call runs the Google Trends Scraper on Apify and is billed to your Apify account, per result:
Per call $0.0025 start fee
Per result $0.002 per search term and data type (the package asks for compact output: one result holds a whole series)
Example interest_over_time() for 3 terms: about $0.0085
Free plan Apify's free plan includes $5 of usage every month: about 600 calls like the one above, no card needed

Put a ceiling on any call with TrendReq(max_charge_usd=0.05).

What is supported

pytrends method pytrends-cloud
build_payload(kw_list, cat, timeframe, geo, gprop) ✅ up to 5 terms, named ranges ("today 5-y", "now 7-d"…) or dates ("2024-01-01 2024-06-30", "2024-01-01T00 2024-01-07T23"), one geo or a list of geos to compare one term across regions
interest_over_time() ✅ same DataFrame: one int column per term, isPartial, date index
interest_by_region(resolution, inc_low_vol, inc_geo_code) ✅ COUNTRY, REGION, CITY, DMA, low-volume regions, geoCode column
related_queries() ✅ {term: {"top": df, "rising": df}}
related_topics() ✅ same shape and columns; Google currently returns no related topics for most searches, so you get None (pytrends raised an IndexError there)
trending_searches(pn) ✅ from Google's daily trending feed; pn is a name ("united_states") or a code ("US")
today_searches(pn) ✅ a Series of today's trending searches
realtime_trending_searches(pn, count) ✅ different columns: title, approxTraffic, pubDate, newsItems (Google retired the realtime endpoint pytrends used)
suggestions, categories, top_charts, multirange_interest_over_time, get_historical_interest ❌ raise NotImplementedError: open an issue if you need one

Differences from pytrends

  • Speed. A data call takes about 5 to 10 seconds, the time of one cloud run. Results are cached per TrendReq, so calling the same method twice runs once.
  • Ignored arguments. tz, timeout, proxies, retries, backoff_factor and requests_args are accepted, so your code runs unchanged, and ignored: the requests to Google are made in the cloud. Use run_timeout (seconds, at most 300) instead.
  • Exceptions. pytrends_cloud.exceptions has the same ResponseError and TooManyRequestsError, plus AuthenticationError for a missing or refused token. If pytrends is still installed, they subclass its own exceptions, so except clauses written against pytrends.exceptions keep catching them.
  • Regions. Inside a country other than the US, resolution="REGION" or "CITY" is applied; pytrends silently ignored it there.
  • No silent zeros. If a run stops early and one of your terms comes back without data while the others have some, you get a ResponseError instead of a column of zeros.

Without Python

The same data (with up to 25 terms per run, schedules, webhooks and exports to CSV, Excel or Google Sheets) is available as an Apify Actor: https://apify.com/bibian/google-trends-scraper

Disclaimer

Not affiliated with Google, nor with the authors of pytrends. Google Trends figures are aggregated and anonymized by Google.

License

MIT
